new_value: {"description":"P3, found during project-LICHEN-worker6-5b1y (the UDP sibling of this divergence). ICMPv6 computed-zero checksum reconstruct convention diverges across implementations: C icmpv6_checksum (lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc_checksum.c:100-106) maps computed-zero to 0xFFFF via finalize_checksum; python icmpv6_checksum (python/src/lichen/ipv6/icmpv6.py:79-88) keeps 0x0000 (raw complement, no or-0xFFFF); rust has TWO icmpv6 checksum helpers: codec.rs icmpv6_checksum_parts (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:650-655) routes through ones_complement_sum which maps zero-\u003e0xFFFF (so the LIVE decompress agrees with C), while headers.rs icmpv6_checksum (rust/lichen-schc/src/headers.rs:237-242) keeps 0x0000 (agrees with python). Correction over the initial description: rust codec.rs DOES map (verified by kimi correctness pass of 5b1y); the divergence is python-vs-C/rust-live on the wire, plus a rust-internal inconsistency between its two checksum helpers. For ICMPv6 a zero checksum is legal (the RFC 8200 8.1 zero-prohibition is UDP-specific) and both wire values verify as valid when the true checksum is zero, so there is no rejection asymmetry - but reconstructed byte streams differ (rule-2 echo round trip of a computed-zero packet: C and rust live path emit 0xFFFF, python emits 0x0000), failing byte-identical round-trip assertions for that packet class (~1/65536 per distinct packet; no existing corpus row hits it - checked: icmpv6 echo vectors have nonzero computed checksums). Fix needs a coordinated convention decision (map or not for ICMPv6 - RFC is silent) applied to C finalize_checksum, python icmpv6, AND BOTH rust helpers (headers.rs icmpv6_checksum plus a decision whether ones_complement_sum should grow a protocol-scoped variant), then pin with a shared rule-2 vector whose ICMPv6 checksum computes to zero. Do NOT scope-creep 5b1y's UDP fix: that one is protocol-correct as-is."}
